chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Knowledge is coupled to deed. So the one who knows, acts; and the one who acts, knows. And knowledge calls out to deed — so if it responds, well and good; otherwise, knowledge departs from him.

key_terms.ارْتَحَلَ: Departed (irtahala) — literally 'journeyed away', implying knowledge withdraws when not acted upon
key_terms.الْعَمَلُ: Deed/action ('amal) — righteous conduct, practice of religious obligations
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: Knowledge ('ilm) — in the Shia tradition, this refers especially to divinely-grounded religious knowledge, not merely secular learning
key_terms.يَهْتِفُ: Calls out/invites (yahtif) — a vivid personification: knowledge actively summons action

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between knowledge and action?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that knowledge and action are intrinsically inseparable — genuine knowledge naturally leads to practice, and authentic practice deepens knowledge. The striking metaphor of knowledge 'departing' from one who fails to act reflects a Shia theological understanding that religious knowledge is not merely intellectual but spiritually transformative, and that failure to act on knowledge causes it to be withdrawn.
